amount_scale: full Ghana cedis as printed - the Act carries no scale factor
doc_locator: Act 1163, Fourth Schedule (Summary of Expenditure by Programme, Economic Item and Funding), vote 026, programme 02602
notes: The only wholly-treasury-financed digital programme in the Ghanaian budget.** Every cedi of it is GoG; the ministry's other digital programme (02603) is 11% treasury. · No compensation of employees at all**, so the whole GHS 100m is spend rather than payroll - unusual in this corpus and the reason the line matters more than its size suggests. · Cross-footed against the Act's own arithmetic: GoG 60,000,000 + 40,000,000 = 100,000,000 = the programme's grand total, and vote 026's five programmes sum to its printed vote total (GHS 1,255,121,769) to one cedi.

The **GHS 138,000,000 donor share** - goods and services 27,600,000, non-financial assets 110,400,000 - is `non-state` and is **not** built as a record: the volume names no funder beyond the column heading `Donors`, so it fails the spec's first fact. notes: Ghana's data protection authority receives no treasury money at all.** Every GoG column on this row - compensation, goods and services, non-financial assets - is blank, and the volume states it in terms: *"The Commission is funded through internally generated funds and has a total staff strength of Thirty-Nine (39) personnel."* The Commission's whole 2026 budget is **GHS 9,720,400**, funded from the fees it charges the data controllers it regulates. That is **1.3% of the programme it sits in** and **0.77% of the ministry's vote**. · This is what `Appropriation (No. 2) Act, 2025 (Act 1163)` could not show.** The Act stops at programme grain and appropriates GHS 729,947,850 to programme 02603 with no sub-programme split, which is why the Data Protection Commission, the Cyber Security Authority and NITA all appeared to have no vote of their own.
